Yeah, I think your diagnosis is right.

At the master commit you linked, the single-zone driver sets `PhysicalTime = TimeIter * dt` during [Preprocess](https://github.com/su2code/SU2/blob/bc15466602a687d6fb796d5df7a12ce3fde0949a/SU2_CFD/src/drivers/CSinglezoneDriver.cpp#L106-L122). That same value is then passed to [`GetMMSSourceTerm`](https://github.com/su2code/SU2/blob/bc15466602a687d6fb796d5df7a12ce3fde0949a/SU2_CFD/src/solvers/CIncEulerSolver.cpp#L1854-L1880), while the dual-time residual treats the current iterate as `U^{n+1}` and forms either the BDF1 or BDF2 time derivative against the stored previous states ([residual assembly](https://github.com/su2code/SU2/blob/bc15466602a687d6fb796d5df7a12ce3fde0949a/SU2_CFD/src/solvers/CIncEulerSolver.cpp#L2837-L2902)).

So for a nonautonomous MMS source, the current sequence is basically

`solve for U^{n+1}` using `f(t_n)`,

which gives exactly the old-time recurrence you measured. It is still first-order consistent under `DT_STEPPING_1ST`, so I would not call the integrator inconsistent, but it is not a backward Euler evaluation of the time-dependent forcing.

The potentially more important case is `DT_STEPPING_2ND`. The state derivative there is BDF2, but if the forcing is still evaluated at `t_n`, then

`f(t_{n+1}) - f(t_n) = O(dt)`,

so the lagged forcing can reduce the temporal convergence to first order for a genuinely time-dependent source. I would include both first- and second-order dual-time cases in the regression.

I would avoid treating the `(TimeIter + 1) * dt` edit as the complete fix. `PhysicalTime` is used for more than the source term: it is also passed into the [verification-solution error calculation](https://github.com/su2code/SU2/blob/bc15466602a687d6fb796d5df7a12ce3fde0949a/SU2_CFD/include/solvers/CFVMFlowSolverBase.inl#L535-L575) and [time-dependent verification boundary states](https://github.com/su2code/SU2/blob/bc15466602a687d6fb796d5df7a12ce3fde0949a/SU2_CFD/include/solvers/CFVMFlowSolverBase.inl#L1518-L1553). Globally advancing it may fix this reproducer while changing output and other semantics elsewhere.

My preference would be to define the time levels explicitly. something like stored-state time versus target/solution time—and use the target time for MMS source and boundary evaluation. Then the output and restart paths can keep whichever convention they require.

tldr; yes, the current source explains your observed recurrence, and the uniform transient MMS case looks like a good regression test. The remaining maintainer question is whether the old-time source evaluation was intentional or is just an ambiguous physical-time convention.
